Several commenters noted confusion with Apache Superset: 'This looks like grafana, right?... I thought this was somehow related to Apache Superset.' The founder admitted: 'bad choice on my part... not thinking about apache superset at all since it was a different domain.'

User comparing to Conductor: 'For me the greatest difference is that superset is terminal-centric while conductor is chat-centric... superset, for me (been using for quite some time now) is basically to organize my agent and terminal sessions per task and project.'
'Very excited about the remote workspaces!... but the typing is quite laggy... have you considered something like mosh?'

'one issue i'm having... in long running terminal sessions I'm getting rendering issues. Like some characters show as something else. I have to resize the window to fix it... I think i also have it more on the big screen (4k) than on the laptop screen.'

Power user praise: 'Now i'm running probably 40-50 agent sessions over several repos simultaneously without any issues and losing track!' after struggling to manage more than ~20 terminal tabs before.
'No linear integration in free version and taxing it 20$/m is a bit steep.'
'Nice work Avi, you got a user out of this message, at least for now. The background service keeping the terminals alive is lovely stuff.'

'Noticed this is built with electron (nice job with the project architecture btw, I appreciate the cleanness), any particular reason a Windows build isn't available yet?' Team responded they focused on macOS first to keep the surface area small.

Founder explained how Superset handles state across worktrees: 'superset manages worktrees + runs setup/teardown scripts you define on project setup. Those scripts can install dependencies, transfer env variables, and spin up branching services.'
'I've used superset at work this last week, and it's great! Excited to see what's next!'
